name: 1801 Prairie Avenue — W. W. Kimball's Chateauesque house in Bedford stone, built on K01 at the massing J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows (T-2538, moved onto the kit by T-2843; refined by T-2910, T-2911, T-2540, T-1890)

function.note: The 1911 sheet marks the building 'D' (dwelling): '3B stone dwelling (D)'. Carried to 1904 on the T-1841 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

research_note: MOVED ONTO K01 BY T-2843 (piece 3 of T-2789), at the massing T-2538 read off J. W. Taylor's photograph of c. 1895 (taylor_c1895_kimball_residence_1801, camera data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/taylor_c1895_northwest.json) and the 1911 sheet 28 trace (s28fp-1801-b1). The draft builder's copy is retired: the house is now an all-stone K01 frontage (T-2788) in Bedford stone, the register's material for it (pa-1801-23): two storeys of wall to a cornice at 8.1 m under steep slate mansard faces to a deck about 16-17 m up; the front's south pavilion and the 18th Street wall's three-storey section on K08 projections carried past the eave to 13.9 m; the round tower on a K08 tower on the 18th Street wall, its cone to about 18.7 m; the gabled section and the east range as slated K01 wings (T-2841). Three things the photograph and the sheet show are not built and each has its ticket: the east range's corner turret (a turret turned round a wing's corner, eaves level with the range's) and the range's south 12 m behind the gabled section (a wing longer than its host wall), both T-2900, and the pavilion's coped gable (T-2540). The corner loggia, its two arches and the swept stair are built (T-2910); the bowed bay, the front's openings and carving are T-2911's; the roof's dormers, cresting, stacks and the flank's gable are T-2540's; T-1890 finishes the architecture. What the build invents is in docs/LIBERTIES.md (L-kimball-1801-k01-2843, after L-kimball-1801-massing-2538) and what differs is open in the match record.

documented_range.note: The record claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building ('3B', stone) and the T-1841 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped); J. W. Taylor's photograph shows it standing about 1895. Its building and loss dates are the finishing ticket's to read (T-1890).

position.symbolic_location: 1801 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_1801 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 18th to 20th Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 28).
position.note: The rear north corner of the K01 main body: the draft's origin, kept (lot frame u 18.000, v -11.500 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the georeference's independent check is 1.47 m RMS. Rotation 179.454 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line, so v runs south from the 18th Street wall and the Taylor camera, solved in this frame, stands unchanged (T-2843).

derivation.reason: The four derivation methods re-derive from the 1835 files; this position is re-derived from the traced sheet and the 1904 parcel by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py --check instead.

footprint.note: The main block on the 1911 sheet's trace (s28fp-1801-b1) in the record's frame (u toward Prairie Avenue from the main block's rear, v south from the 18th Street wall): the 18th Street wall at v 0, the front at u 20.5 (the trace's front runs at u 20.6-20.7 either side of the bowed bay's bulge), and the south wall at v 11.0, where the trace runs from the front back to u 6.9 (v 10.99-11.04) and where the Taylor camera's south-west bearing lands (v 11.2). T-2538's draft fitted the largest rectangle inside the trace (v 0-9.75) and stood its south pavilion past it; K01 builds the pavilion as a projection on the front, flush with this corner, so the block takes the trace's own width. Behind u 6.9 the trace steps in to v 9.5-10.9 on a side the camera does not see; the block runs straight there (L-kimball-1801-k01-2843).

stories.note: The 1911 sheet prints '3B': three storeys over a basement. The Taylor photograph shows two storeys of wall to the main cornice at about 8.1 m and the third in the steep roof over the main block; the pavilion, the flank section and the gabled section carry the third as a wall storey (form.bays, form.rear_wings).

construction.note: The sheet's colours read 'stone' and the photograph shows the front and the 18th Street flank laid alike in ashlar: an all-stone house (T-2788), its K02 courses round every face.

principal_floor_m.note: The front stair's nine risers of about 0.16 m, read through the solved camera (T-2538).

storey_heights_m.note: Read through the solved camera (T-2538): the band over the principal storey at about 4.8-5.0 m and the main cornice at 8.0-8.2 m, so 3.55 m and 3.1 m from the 1.45 m floor to an eave at 8.1 m.

wall_thickness_front_m.note: A stone front's thickness in the K01 range, as 1811's.

wall_thickness_side_m.note: An all-stone house's side walls as thick as its front: the photograph shows the flank in the same ashlar.

service_wall_brick.note: The kit names its K03 panel; an all-stone house lays no brick face with it.

stone_front.note: Bedford stone, the register's material for 1801 (frontage register row pa-1801-23, K02's limestone_bedford), laid in smooth courses as the photograph shows on the front and the flank alike, over a two-course base to the basement lights' heads. The front's carved frieze, string courses and corbel table are T-2911's and T-2540's.

street_front_trim.note: Plain stone lintels: the photograph's carved pilasters and moulded surrounds are T-2922's.

roof_form.note: Very steep slate faces from the cornice to a deck ringed with cresting about 17 m up, as the photograph shows (T-2538).

roof_pitch_deg.note: The deck behind the cresting is not seen from the street; a low hip inside the K05 mansard's upper range.

eave_overhang_m.note: The cornice's projection, inside the mansard's range.

mansard.note: Read through the solved camera (T-2538): straight steep faces at about 72 degrees from the 8.1 m cornice to a curb 7.2 m higher, so the deck's front edge reads 15.3-16.3 m up, inside the photograph's 15.5-17 m. A face this tall holds the house's third storey and its attic, which is why it passes K05's attic-storey 4.5 m (T-2843 lets a mansard that holds two storeys rise to 7.5 m). The face's two tiers of hooded dormers and the deck's cresting are T-2540's.

stair_tread_m.note: T-2910: the flight's nine risers come down about 2.5 m in front of the loggia's arch, read through the solved camera to the cheeks' foot blocks (the left about 1.9 m out, the right about 2.4 m), so eight treads of about 0.28 m off a 0.3 m landing. Graded reconstructed as a whole: its places and sizes are read off the photograph, and what the photograph cannot give is invented within them (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kimball-1801-loggia-2910).

stair_landing_depth_m.note: T-2910: the photograph's flight starts at the arch: the loggia's floor is the landing, and the cheeks run level only a short way before they sweep down. A 0.3 m step at the arch's mouth, the rest of the landing the loggia's own floor behind it. Graded reconstructed as a whole: its places and sizes are read off the photograph, and what the photograph cannot give is invented within them (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kimball-1801-loggia-2910).

stoop_width_m.note: T-2910: the flight is as wide as the loggia behind the arch, its cheeks' inner faces about at the arch's piers (v 0.45-2.75 through the camera, the left cheek outside the corner pier's face). Built 2.3 m between 0.3 m cheeks, the room's own width. Graded reconstructed as a whole: its places and sizes are read off the photograph, and what the photograph cannot give is invented within them (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kimball-1801-loggia-2910).

entrance_bay.note: The photograph's entrance is under the loggia at the front's 18th Street end (K01's 'south' end of the front in this frame, whose v runs south from 18th Street). T-2910 builds the loggia's arches and the swept stair there.

front_bays.note: The door at the 18th Street end under the loggia (1.6) and the bowed bay's centre (5.05), so the second storey's one window over the loggia stands at 1.6 and the bay's own lights replace the draft's two evenly spaced sash a storey (T-2921); a bay's centre on the front cuts no wall window behind it. The carved surrounds are T-2922's.

side_bays.note: The 18th Street wall's openings clear of the flank section and the tower; their sizes and heads are T-2911's. T-2910: the principal storey's opening at 18.9 m is the loggia's side arch (the photograph's), so that storey has no window there; the window over it is the photograph's.

north_bays.note: The south wall, toward 1811, which no picture shows.

rear_bays.note: The rear wall south of the gabled section, which no picture shows.

sash_by_storey.note: The flank's windows read about 1.2 m wide through the solved camera (good to a few centimetres at that range), built at the K01 contract's widest ordinary sash, 1.15 m; their heights and sills reconstructed.

basement_lights.note: Under the principal floor, their heads on the base's coping.

roof_covering.note: Slate on the steep faces, as the photograph shows; the deck behind the cresting reconstructed as tin.

chimneys.note: One stack on the south wall, which no picture shows; the pavilion's and the flank's tall stacks in the photograph are T-2540's.

rainwater.note: The kit's copper gutter behind the cornice, its downpipes on the south and rear walls, which no picture shows; the photograph shows none on the front or the 18th Street flank.

window_kit.note: The district's two-over-two sash; the plate's sash is too small to count lights.

entrance_kit.note: T-2910 builds the corner loggia J. W. Taylor's c. 1895 photograph shows at the front's 18th Street end, read through its solved camera (data/reference_views/kimball_house_1801_prairie/taylor_c1895_northwest.json): a round arch on the front and one on the 18th Street face, each about 1.9 m across (the front's void x 1010-1095 on the print, v 0.5-2.7; the flank's u 18.1-19.5 inside its surround), centred about 1.6 m from the corner, springing about 2.65 m over grade and crowned about 3.6 m (the photograph's 2.61-2.67 and 3.57), so 2.15 m over the 1.45 m floor; through the 18th Street arch the loggia's back wall and its door frame are seen about on the front arch's axis. Built as K07's deep-arched double door made a loggia: the front arch (opening_m) under its voussoir block, a room 2.3 m square behind it (v 0.45-2.75, 2.75 m behind the front) on the door's floor, the double door in its back wall, and the side arch cut through the 18th Street wall with its own voussoir block, laid in that wall's courses; under the side arch the photograph's stone balcony, its top the arch's sill and its underside corbelled back into the wall. The stair comes down the front out of the arch, as broad as the room, between cheeks whose tops run level by the arch and sweep down in one reversed curve to a block at the foot about 0.85 m over grade (the photograph's left foot block reads 0.68-0.70 m over the walk at the camera's grade, which stands about 0.2 m under the lot's). Reconstructed, and recorded in docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kimball-1801-loggia-2910: the room's depth, ceiling and square plan (only its back wall and the door's frame are seen), the door's leaves and transom, the cheeks' thickness, the balcony's projection and corbel, and plain stone where the photograph shows carved panels on the piers, the cheeks' blocks and the balcony's face (T-2911 and T-2540 carry the carving). front_yard_m is the 7.7 m from the front to the lot line (street_u 28.2). Graded reconstructed as a whole: its places and sizes are read off the photograph, and what the photograph cannot give is invented within them (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kimball-1801-loggia-2910).

bays.note: Read through the Taylor camera (T-2538) and the 1911 sheet's trace, built on K08 (T-2843). p_south: the front's south pavilion, three storeys of wall to about 13.9 m, flush with the south corner as the photograph shows it (its face from about x 1235 to the corner's x 1345 on the print, so v 7.3-11.2 through the camera; built 3.6 m wide on the 11.0 m block), its storeys 5.0, 3.1 and 5.8 m from grade to the main cornice's line and the gable's springing. p_flank: the 18th Street wall's three-storey section with the corbel table, between the gabled section and the tower, to the same 13.9 m; the photograph's section runs about 7.8 m (u 2.2-10 at the camera) and K08's widest pavilion is 6.0 m, so it is built 6.0 m wide against the tower (u 5.1-11.1). Both stand 0.6 m proud (K08's own pavilion depth, the least its window recesses fit in), where the trace draws the pavilion at 0-0.4 m and the flank section at about 0.1 m, which also lets the main cornice's 0.3 m eave die behind their faces; over the eave each is closed on the wall plane (T-2843). Their caps are K08's low hip: the pavilion's coped stone gable (apex about 17 m) and the section's roof are T-2540's. tower: the round tower on the 18th Street wall, its axis 12.6 m from the main block's rear (between the photograph's u 13.0 and the sheet's bump at u 12.0), 1.45 m in radius, its eaves 12.9 m and its cone 5.8 m more to about 18.7 m with a finial, as the photograph reads; its centre 0.1 m out of the wall's face (the least that keeps its finial clear of the wall), so it stands 1.55 m proud where the sheet draws its bump 1.2-1.3 m out. One shaft for the photograph's shaft and corbelled upper stage. The tower's and the flank section's windows are the kit's sash at about the photograph's places. p_south's windows (T-2921): the photograph shows one mullioned and transomed pair a storey on the pavilion's face, about 2.4 m across between its carved pilasters (70 px of the face's 205), built as K06's plate-glass casement pair under a stone transom, 2.0 m clear on its 0.18 m mullion, centred as the photograph centres it; the principal storey's from 1.75 m (0.3 m over the floor; the print's sill at y 1000) 2.45 m tall, the second storey's from 5.6 m 2.2 m tall (its head a little over the bow's, as the print draws the two, and its frame inside the storey's clear wall under the 8.1 m eave), the third's 1.8 m from 8.8 m. The transom lights' small leaded glazing is not built. front_bow (T-2921): the photograph's bowed bay between the loggia and the pavilion, two storeys under a stone balcony. Its north junction at x 1130 and its silhouette's south edge against the pavilion's pilaster at x 1245 place it through the camera: built 3.4 m on its chord centred at v 5.05 (v 3.35-6.75, 0.65 m short of the pavilion's cheek) and 0.8 m out, and its render's outline falls within about 5 px of the print's at both edges. The sheet's bulge at v 4.8-10.2 is wider and further south; the photograph is the later and closer evidence, so the bay stands where the photograph has it. One broad light a storey, 1.5 m clear, set 20 degrees round the bow toward 18th Street, where the print shows each light filling the face it sees (x 1153-1230; at the crown the render put it 30 px south of the print's): the principal storey's 2.4 m from 1.75 m with a 0.7 m transom light over a 0.12 m bar (the print's bar about 0.8 m under the head), the second storey's 2.15 m from 5.4 m with a 0.6 m transom light. The bow is carried up 0.6 m past the house's eave, to 8.7 m, because the print wraps the main cornice round it over a frieze about 1.2 m deep above the second storey's heads (the build's main cornice stays at 8.1 m, T-2540's); its eaves are K10's moulded stone cornice swept round the bow, and on it a stone balustrade 0.6 m high round the bow from wall to wall, the print's coping at about y 535. The balustrade (T-2930): the print's pierced stone panels between posts, the one post it shows between the north wall's (x 1132) and the pavilion's pilaster (x 1231) standing at x 1186-1190, where a post a quarter of the way round the bow falls in the render (x 1191) and a post on its crown would fall at x 1247; so four panels between five posts, the crown's and the south quarter's hidden from this camera behind the pavilion's pilaster. Each panel is pierced right through in a diagonal lattice, two staggered rows of upright diamonds with half-diamonds against the coping and the base, about five across a panel (the right one at x 1191-1226, y 537-560 on the 1600 px print); the quatrefoils T-2922's title named cannot be told from diamonds at the print's 5-6 px a piercing. Built as K08's stone balustrade with panels: a 0.13 m coping, a 0.10 m base course on the cornice and 0.37 m of lattice between them (the print's about 8, 6 and 22 px of its 36), straps 0.05 m square crossing at 0.16 m along the bow. The straps' section and pitch, the posts' plain faces and the panels' depth are reconstructed within those sizes (L-kimball-1801-bow-lattice-2930). T-2931 (piece 2 of T-2922): the Taylor print's carved pilasters, one a storey at the bow's north junction (x 1127-1137) and at each corner of the pavilion's face (x 1232-1250 and 1322-1340), each under a capital below the band over it (the principal storey's at y 828-848) with a chain of carved lozenges down its shaft, the principal storey's from the windows' sill line on a corbel hanging under it (y 995-1018); and the moulded frame round every light of the bow and every pair of the pavilion under a projecting head. Built as K08's pilasters (0.22 m on the bow's ends, the hidden south one as the north; 0.30 m on the pavilion's) and K08's window surrounds (0.12 and 0.20 m jambs under 0.22 and 0.20 m hoods); their sections, the capitals' plain blocks for the print's carved ones and the lozenges are reconstructed (L-kimball-1801-pilasters-2931).

rear_wings.note: The sheet's two rectangles behind the main block, in the trace's own lines (T-2843), with the walls and roofs the Taylor photograph shows on the 18th Street flank. r3: the gabled section, u -8.5 to 0 and v 0 to 6.0 where the trace's south line steps in (the draft's fit stood it 0.5 m off the 18th Street wall, which the trace and the photograph run straight), three storeys to 13.9 m under a 45-degree slate hip, its apex about 16.9 m (the photograph's gable facing 18th Street with its balcony is T-2540's). r2: the east range, two storeys to 8.1 m (the photograph's eaves about 8.2 m) under a 45-degree slate hip, from u -8.5 back to the trace's rear at u -17.9, where the camera's bearing also puts the flank's east end (the draft's fit stopped at u -17.0). It is built v 0 to 6.0 only: a K01 wing stands inside its host wall's length, and the trace's range runs on south to v 18.3 behind a gabled section 6 m wide, so the south 12 m of it waits on that kit piece (T-2900). Its north-east corner turret is not built: the photograph shows its eaves level with the range's, a turret turned round the wing's corner rather than a K08 tower past its eave (T-2842's rule), and that is a kit piece of its own (T-2900). Openings are the kit's sash at reconstructed places.
